style="font-size:32px;font-weight:900;line-height:1.15">Why pros book La Ventana for the season</h2></div></div><div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-6 lg:gap-8"><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-md border border-[var(--color-border)]"><p class="text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.2em] text-[var(--color-teal)] font-semibold">Distance to launch</p><p class="mt-3 font-display text-2xl text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-weight:900">5-min walk</p><p class="mt-2 text-sm text-[var(--color-soft-gray)] leading-relaxed">Town launch is straight down the road from our front door. El Sargento (slightly north) is just north of town and often works better for advanced riders depending on conditions.</p></div></div></div></div></section><div aria-hidden="true" style="background:var(--color-bg-soft);line-height:0"><svg viewBox="0 0 1440 80" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" preserveAspectRatio="none" class="block w-full h-12 sm:h-16"></svg></div><section class="mx-auto max-w-3xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 py-14"><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><h2 class="font-display text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-size:28px;font-weight:900">The lay of the land</h2><div class="mt-6 space-y-5 text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-size:15px;line-height:30px;font-weight:300"><p>La Ventana is a small fishing village turned kite town on the Sea of Cortez side of southern Baja, about 45 minutes by car from La Paz International Airport (LAP). During the core wind season, the El Norte often builds from late morning into the afternoon. The geography is what makes the bay work: desert hills behind town, broad beach access, and Sea of Cortez water in front of you.</p><p>The result is a side-onshore wind on flat-to-rolling water, the kind of conditions advanced riders use for big-air sessions and beginners use to build real water time with a school. Conditions still change day by day, so local forecasts matter.</p><p>The launches: <strong>Playa Central</strong> and the main town beach are the easiest places to orient yourself. <strong>El Sargento</strong> is just north of La Ventana and can be a better fit for advanced riders depending on wind, swell, and crowds.</p><p>What you don&#x27;t get in La Ventana is consistent surf-style wave riding; for that, ask about Pacific-side day trips. What you do get is a strong winter wind culture, schools, rentals, and plenty of travelers planning their days around the forecast.</p></div></div></section><div aria-hidden="true" style="background:var(--color-bg);line-height:0"><svg viewBox="0 0 1440 80" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" preserveAspectRatio="none" class="block w-full h-12 sm:h-16"></svg></div><section class="bg-[var(--color-bg-soft)]"><div class="mx-auto max-w-3xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 py-16"><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><div class="text-center mb-10"><span class="eyebrow-script">things kiters ask</span><h2 class="font-display text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-size:32px;font-weight:900">Kite FAQ</h2></div></div><ul class="space-y-6"><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><li class="border-b border-[var(--color-border)] pb-5"><h3 class="font-display text-lg text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-weight:700">When is the kite season in La Ventana?</h3><p class="mt-2 text-sm text-[var(--color-soft-gray)] leading-relaxed">Peak El Norte season usually runs November through March. Some local operators describe the wider wind window as mid-October through mid-April, but current forecasts matter more than the calendar.</p></li></div><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><li class="border-b border-[var(--color-border)] pb-5"><h3 class="font-display text-lg text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-weight:700">Where are the kite launches?</h3><p class="mt-2 text-sm text-[var(--color-soft-gray)] leading-relaxed">Playa Central and the main town beach launches are a short walk from the hotel. El Sargento is slightly north and can be a better fit for advanced riders depending on the day.</p></li></div><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><li class="border-b border-[var(--color-border)] pb-5"><h3 class="font-display text-lg text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-weight:700">Do you store kite gear?</h3><p class="mt-2 text-sm text-[var(--color-soft-gray)] leading-relaxed">Ask the team before you arrive and they can point you to the best place for your gear. Please don&#x27;t lay wet kites on the rooftop deck.</p></li></div><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><li class="border-b border-[var(--color-border)] pb-5"><h3 class="font-display text-lg text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-weight:700">Can you recommend kite schools?</h3><p class="mt-2 text-sm text-[var(--color-soft-gray)] leading-relaxed">We work with several reputable schools in town for IKO-certified lessons (beginner through advanced) and gear rental. Message us a few weeks before your trip and we&#x27;ll point you to whoever&#x27;s running good lessons that season.</p></li></div><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><li class="border-b border-[var(--color-border)] pb-5"><h3 class="font-display text-lg text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-weight:700">What size kite should I bring?</h3><p class="mt-2 text-sm text-[var(--color-soft-gray)] leading-relaxed">Most traveling kiters bring a small quiver rather than one kite. Wind strength changes by rider weight and the day, so check the forecast and ask a local school before packing around one size.</p></li></div><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><li class="border-b border-[var(--color-border)] pb-5"><h3 class="font-display text-lg text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-weight:700">Wing-foiling?</h3><p class="mt-2 text-sm text-[var(--color-soft-gray)] leading-relaxed">Yes — wing-foiling uses the same general wind season and many of the same beach areas. Bring your own gear or rent locally.</p></li></div><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><li class="border-b border-[var(--color-border)] pb-5"><h3 class="font-display text-lg text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-weight:700">Are there tides to worry about?</h3><p class="mt-2 text-sm text-[var(--color-soft-gray)] leading-relaxed">For most kiters, the daily wind forecast matters more than the tide. Check current conditions on a wind app or with a local school before each session.</p></li></div></ul></div></section><div aria-hidden="true" style="background:var(--color-bg-soft);line-height:0"><svg viewBox="0 0 1440 80" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" preserveAspectRatio="none" class="block w-full h-12 sm:h-16"></svg></div><section class="mx-auto max-w-3xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 py-16 text-center"><div style="opacity:0;transform:translateY(28px)"><h2 class="font-display text-[var(--color-ink)]" style="font-size:32px;font-weight:900;line-height:1.15">Ready for the <span class="hl-sun">season?</span></h2><p class="mt-4 text-sm text-[var(--color-soft-gray)] max-w-md mx-auto leading-relaxed">Private rooms book out 4–6 weeks ahead for kite season.
